chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Sahl from his father from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) about a man who entered Mecca performing Tamattuʾ (or Qirān/Ifrād contextually implying missing the standing) for Hajj, and feared that the two standings (Mawqifān) would be missed by him. He said: 'He has his day until the sunrise of the Day of Nahr (10th Dhu al-Hijjah). When the sun rises, he has no Hajj.'
I said: 'What should he do with his Ihram?' He said: 'He should go to Mecca and perform Tawaf around the House and Saʿy between Ṣafā and Marwah.'

I said to him: 'When he does that, what does he do after?' He said: 'If he wishes, he stays in Mecca; and if he wishes, he returns to the people at Minā and is not one of them in anything (i.e., not bound by their specific rituals). If he wishes, he returns to his family, and Hajj is incumbent upon him next year.'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَانِ: The two standings (at Arafat and Muzdalifah), essential pillars of Hajj
key_terms.يَسْعَى: He performs Sa'y (walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.يَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ: He performs Tawaf (circumambulation) of the Kaaba
key_terms.يَوْمِ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses the standing at Arafat and Muzdalifah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific legal consequence of missing the 'Mawqifān' (standings at Arafat and Muzdalifah) for a Mufrid (pilgrim performing Hajj only). The Imam establishes that the Hajj becomes invalid (*Hajj Qadha*) upon sunrise of the Day of Nahr, requiring the pilgrim to perform Tawaf and Sa'y as compensatory acts before departing, thereby distinguishing this scenario from a complete Hajj. This ruling underscores the critical nature of the Arafat standing in Shia jurisprudence, where its absence necessitates a full repetition of the ritual in the following year.
